study type: In vitro experimental study with human tissue analysis (case-control)
exposure: Extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules (collagen I, collagen IV, fibronectin, laminin)
outcome: Trophoblast epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition markers (N-cadherin, vimentin, integrin b1, snail, matrix metalloproteinase-2, zonula occludens-1)
cohort: Tissue samples were obtained from patients undergoing cesarean hysterectomy due to postpartum hemorrhage from placenta accreta spectrum (n=15) or uterine atony (control group; n=10).
finding: ECM molecules in decidua and myometrium induce trophoblast HtrA4 expression, which promotes trophoblast proliferation and invasion, while decidual HtrA1 inhibits HtrA4-induced invasion, indicating reciprocal effects of HtrA4 and HtrA1 are involved in the pathogenesis of placenta accreta spectrum.
cross-section timing: Tissue samples were collected at the time of cesarean hysterectomy due to postpartum hemorrhage.
